title: Gluten-Free Sweet Potato and Corn Waffles
changes_from_base: A gluten-free batter of corn flour, sorghum flour and cornflour, spiced and sweetened with dark brown sugar and bound with mashed roasted sweet potato and oil instead of buttermilk and butter.
summary: A soft, naturally sweet waffle built on roasted sweet potato and a blend of gluten-free flours, finished with maple syrup.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: medium sweet potato (about 350 g), for 240 g mashed flesh
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Prick 1 medium sweet potato and roast at 200°C until very soft, about 45-50 min, then cool and mash 240 g of the flesh until smooth.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Lower the oven to 95°C with a wire rack set in a baking tray inside, then heat the waffle iron and brush it lightly with 1 tsp oil.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk 128 g corn flour, 57 g sorghum flour, 71 g cornflour, 2 tbsp dark brown sugar, 1 tbsp pumpkin pie spice, 3 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp fine salt and ½ tsp xanthan gum in a large bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In a separate bowl whisk 300 ml milk with the mashed sweet potato, 2 eggs and 60 ml vegetable oil until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and whisk until smooth.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Ladle batter into the hot iron and cook until crisp and golden brown.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Move cooked waffles to the rack in the oven to keep warm while the rest cook.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with 60 ml maple syrup and 15 g butter if liked.

tips: Mash the sweet potato while still warm so it blends into the batter without lumps.
Check that the corn flour, sorghum flour, baking powder and spice blend are all labelled gluten-free if that matters to your guests.
Keep cooked waffles on a rack rather than stacked so steam escapes and they stay crisp.
storage: These waffles are best eaten freshly cooked; if you must keep extras, store them covered in the fridge and warm them through in a toaster before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
